<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918160_theRebbe_102" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918160_theRebbe_102__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Introductory header with the Torah portion and date.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbat Parshat Shemini,</t>
    <t s="2">Rosh Chodesh blessing and eve of Rosh Chodesh Iyar, 5728.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Explains the verse "Vayomer lo Yonatan machar chodesh v'nifkadeta ki yifaked moshavecha" and the Rebbe Maharash's interpretation linking "nifkadeta" to both remembrance and union, and "yifaked" to lack, connecting this to the union of Zeir Anpin and Malchut through the concealment of the moon and the drawing down of Keter.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And Yonatan said to him: Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed (v'nifkadeta), for your seat will be vacant (yifaked moshavecha)."</t>
    <t s="1">And the Rebbe Maharash brings</t>
    <t s="2">[the master of the birthday of 2 Iyar]</t>
    <t s="3">in his discourse on this verse,</t>
    <t s="4">that Rashi explains on the verse that "v'nifkadeta" is an expression of remembrance, and "yifaked" is an expression of lack,</t>
    <t s="5">and the interpretation of "v'nifkadeta ki yifaked moshavecha" is,</t>
    <t s="6">that through the vacating of Dovid's place of sitting,</t>
    <t s="7">through this Shaul will remember him.</t>
    <t s="8">And he continues in the discourse,</t>
    <t s="9">that the reason it says "v'nifkadeta"</t>
    <t s="10">(and not "v'nizkarta" or the like),</t>
    <t s="11">is that "v'nifkadeta" is</t>
    <t s="12">(also)</t>
    <t s="13">an expression of union,</t>
    <t s="14">[as the language of our sages,</t>
    <t s="15">"A man is obligated to be intimate (lifkod) with his wife," etc.],</t>
    <t s="16">for Shaul is Binah</t>
    <t s="17">(as it is written,</t>
    <t s="18">"Shaul from Rechovot HaNahar"),</t>
    <t s="19">the root of the emotions of Zeir Anpin</t>
    <t s="20">[as it is written,</t>
    <t s="21">"Who created these (Mi bara eileh),</t>
    <t s="22">"Mi,"</t>
    <t s="23">Binah,</t>
    <t s="24">is the root of "Eileh,"</t>
    <t s="25">the emotions],</t>
    <t s="26">and Dovid is Malchut,</t>
    <t s="27">therefore it says "v'nifkadeta,"</t>
    <t s="28">that Shaul will be intimate with (yifkod) Dovid,</t>
    <t s="29">meaning there will be a union of Zeir Anpin</t>
    <t s="30">[whose root is from Binah,</t>
    <t s="31">Shaul]</t>
    <t s="32">and Malchut</t>
    <t s="33">[Dovid].</t>
    <t s="34">And this is the connection of "v'nifkadeta ki yifaked moshavecha" with "machar chodesh,"</t>
    <t s="35">for on the eve of Rosh Chodesh is the concealment and hiding of the moon,</t>
    <t s="36">until in the moment before the molad not even a point remains of it,</t>
    <t s="37">and through this</t>
    <t s="38">afterwards</t>
    <t s="39">(tomorrow)</t>
    <t s="40">it becomes a new month (chodesh),</t>
    <t s="41">a renewed birth of the moon (molad halevanah),</t>
    <t s="42">the union of the sun and the moon.</t>
    <t s="43">And likewise is it with Malchut</t>
    <t s="44">(the root of the moon),</t>
    <t s="45">that specifically through "yifaked moshavecha"</t>
    <t s="46">(of Dovid,</t>
    <t s="47">Malchut),</t>
    <t s="48">through this is "v'nifkadeta,"</t>
    <t s="49">the union of Malchut with Zeir Anpin.</t>
    <t s="50">And seemingly, one should add,</t>
    <t s="51">that this which on Rosh Chodesh the union of the sun</t>
    <t s="52">(Zeir Anpin)</t>
    <t s="53">and the moon</t>
    <t s="54">(Malchut) occurs,</t>
    <t s="55">is</t>
    <t s="56">that which is drawn into the sun</t>
    <t s="57">(Zeir Anpin)</t>
    <t s="58">from the aspect that is above the sun,</t>
    <t s="59">Keter which is above the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="60">As it is written,</t>
    <t s="61">"With the crown (atarah) with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding,"</t>
    <t s="62">that in order for there to be a union of Zeir Anpin with Malchut</t>
    <t s="63">(the day of his wedding)</t>
    <t s="64">it is through the drawing down into him of the crown (atarah),</t>
    <t s="65">Keter.</t>
    <t s="66">And the drawing down of Keter into Zeir Anpin</t>
    <t s="67">(on the day of his wedding)</t>
    <t s="68">is through Binah,</t>
    <t s="69">"the crown with which his mother crowned him."</t>
    <t s="70">And based on this, the connection of "machar chodesh" with "v'nifkadeta ki yifaked moshavecha" is even more understood,</t>
    <t s="71">for the matter of "machar chodesh"</t>
    <t s="72">[that through the concealment and hiding of the moon</t>
    <t s="73">(on the eve of Rosh Chodesh)</t>
    <t s="74">there occurs</t>
    <t s="75">(on Rosh Chodesh)</t>
    <t s="76">the union of the sun and the moon],</t>
    <t s="77">is,</t>
    <t s="78">because the nullification of the moon</t>
    <t s="79">(that it is concealed and hidden until not even a point remains of it)</t>
    <t s="80">reaches the aspect of Keter which is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="81">from which is drawn</t>
    <t s="82">(through Binah)</t>
    <t s="83">the power for the union of the sun and the moon.</t>
    <t s="84">And likewise is the matter of "v'nifkadeta ki yifaked moshavecha,"</t>
    <t s="85">that through the vacating of Dovid's place of sitting</t>
    <t s="86">(Malchut),</t>
    <t s="87">through this there will be the "v'nifkadeta" of Dovid by Shaul,</t>
    <t s="88">the drawing down of Binah</t>
    <t s="89">(Shaul from Rechovot HaNahar),</t>
    <t s="90">and through this – the drawing down of Keter</t>
    <t s="91">("with the crown with which his mother crowned him").</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Raises the difficulty that "v'nifkadeta" (remembrance/union) and "yifaked" (lack) are opposites, questioning how lack can cause union, and notes that the wording "yifaked" implies the lack itself contains an element of union.</sectionSummary>
    <t s="0">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="1">that "v'nifkadeta" [which is] an expression of remembrance and an expression of being visited (pekidah)</t>
    <t s="2">(union)</t>
    <t s="3">and "yifaked" [which is] an expression of lack are seemingly two opposites,</t>
    <t s="4">and how is it possible that through "yifaked" there will be "v'nifkadeta."</t>
    <t s="5">And even though "yifaked moshavecha"</t>
    <t s="6">(that his place of sitting is lacking)</t>
    <t s="7">is connected with the matter of nullification (bittul),</t>
    <t s="8">and nullification reaches Keter</t>
    <t s="9">(as above)</t>
    <t s="10">from which the power for union is drawn,</t>
    <t s="11">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="12">from the fact that the interpretation of "yifaked moshavecha" is that your seat will be lacking,</t>
    <t s="13">it implies,</t>
    <t s="14">that this "yifaked moshavecha" is a reason for "v'nifkadeta"</t>
    <t s="15">("v'nifkadeta ki yifaked moshavecha")</t>
    <t s="16">is</t>
    <t s="17">(not only because "yifaked moshavecha" is connected with the matter of nullification,</t>
    <t s="18">but also)</t>
    <t s="19">that "yifaked moshavecha" itself</t>
    <t s="20">(that your seat will be lacking)</t>
    <t s="21">is a reason for "v'nifkadeta,"</t>
    <t s="22">and it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="23">how is it possible that "yifaked," an expression of lack, brings about "v'nifkadeta."</t>
    <t s="24">And likewise it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="25">from the fact that it says "yifaked moshavecha"</t>
    <t s="26">(and not "yechsar moshavecha"),</t>
    <t s="27">an expression of pekidah (visitation/union),</t>
    <t s="28">it implies,</t>
    <t s="29">that the connection of "yifaked" to "v'nifkadeta" is</t>
    <t s="30">(not only that "yifaked" brings about "v'nifkadeta,"</t>
    <t s="31">but)</t>
    <t s="32">that in "yifaked" itself there is</t>
    <t s="33">(concealed)</t>
    <t s="34">the matter of "v'nifkadeta."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
